How Many Days Between Dates Calculator

Use our free How Many Days Between Dates Calculator to quickly find out the exact number of days between two dates. Simply enter your start date and end date and the calculator will work out the difference for you.

How Many Days Are Between Two Dates?

Wondering how many days are between two dates? Our date calculator makes it simple to find the answer without manually counting the days on a calendar.

Enter any two dates to calculate the number of days between them, whether you're checking how long has passed since an event, counting down to an important date or working out the duration of a particular period.

Calculate the Number of Days Between Dates

Calculating the number of days between dates can be difficult when the dates fall in different months or years. Our date difference calculator automatically works out the difference, taking account of the different lengths of each month and leap years.

Simply select your two dates and the calculator will show you how many days separate them.

How to Calculate Days Between Two Dates

To calculate the days between two dates, choose the start date and end date using the calculator above. The calculator then determines the exact difference between the two dates.

For example, you could enter 1 January as the start date and 1 February as the end date to find out how many days are between the two dates. The calculator does the date calculation automatically, saving you from counting manually.

How Many Days Until a Date?

You can also use the calculator to work out how many days until a date. Enter today's date as the starting date and your future date as the end date to calculate the number of days remaining.

This can be useful when counting down to birthdays, holidays, deadlines, events, appointments or other important dates.

How Many Days Have Passed Since a Date?

To find out how many days have passed since a date, enter the earlier date as your start date and today's date as the end date. The calculator will show the number of days between the two dates.

This can be useful for tracking project durations, subscriptions, anniversaries and other periods of time.

In the UK the sun rises before 5am and sets after 9pm in the south, and further north the daylight lasts even longer, with the sky barely getting dark in Shetland.

Thousands of people gather at Stonehenge in Wiltshire each year to watch the sunrise on the solstice, and midsummer is celebrated across Scandinavia and much of Europe with bonfires and dancing.

Clocks Go Forward Countdown (UK)

Our Clocks Go Forward Countdown (UK) shows exactly how long is left until the clocks going forward. The live timer counts down the days, hours, minutes and seconds to 1am on the last Sunday in March.

In the UK the clocks go forward by one hour at 1am on the last Sunday in March, when Greenwich Mean Time changes to British Summer Time. The clocks change at 1am, so the night is an hour shorter, but the evenings are lighter for the rest of the spring and summer. The saying "spring forward, fall back" helps to remember which way they go.

British Summer Time was introduced in 1916, following a campaign by the builder William Willett, who argued that people were wasting daylight in summer mornings.

Our Leap Day Countdown shows exactly how long is left until the next Leap Day. The live timer counts down the days, hours, minutes and seconds to 29 February in leap years.

A Leap Day is the extra day, 29 February, added to the calendar in most years divisible by four to keep it in step with the Earth's orbit around the sun. A year takes about 365.2422 days, so without a leap day the calendar would drift by about a day every four years. Years divisible by 100 are not leap years unless they are also divisible by 400, so 2000 was a leap year but 1900 and 2100 are not.

People born on 29 February are known as leaplings or leapers, and often celebrate their birthday on 28 February or 1 March in other years. In some traditions, leap day is the one day when women may propose marriage.

Pregnancy Due Date Countdown

Counting down to your due date

If you know your due date, enter it above. If you only know the first day of your last period, enter that instead and the due date is worked out for you, and the other way round. Whichever box you edited last is the one that is used. The counter shows the time left to your due date and how many weeks and days pregnant you are.

How the due date is worked out

A full-term pregnancy is about 40 weeks, or 280 days, from the first day of the last menstrual period, the rule used by doctors and midwives. It assumes a cycle of about 28 days, so the date is an estimate. Only around 5% of babies arrive on their due date, and it is normal for babies to arrive in the weeks either side.

Your midwife's date

The date given after your dating scan is the one to use, because scans are more accurate than dates from your last period. This tool is not medical advice, so speak to your midwife or doctor about your pregnancy.
